summary.text: Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are neither mirror images of each other nor identical.
They differ in configuration at one or more, but not all, of the related stereocenters, whereas enantiomers differ at every stereocenter.
Diastereomers have different physical properties and often different chemical reactivity, as glucose and galactose show.

facts.label: One-center difference
facts.value: Diastereomers that differ at only one stereocenter are epimers

facts.label: Three stereocenters
facts.value: Eight stereoisomers, from 2ⁿ for n chiral centers

facts.label: Threonine's partner
facts.value: Its diastereomer allothreonine is very rare in nature

items.prompt: A chemist compares two stereoisomers of one compound and finds they are not mirror images and not the same molecule. What is their relationship?
A molecule has three stereocenters and no meso form. How many stereoisomers should a chemist expect?
items.explain: The number of stereoisomers is 2ⁿ, so three stereocenters give eight.

items.prompt: Glucose and galactose weigh the same per mole, yet the body absorbs galactose slightly faster. What explains the difference?

options.label: They are enantiomers with identical properties
They are diastereomers that differ in stability
They are the same molecule in disguise

items.explain: They are diastereomers; glucose is more stable than galactose, and that difference makes galactose absorbed slightly faster.

items.prompt: A compound has several stereocenters. Each of its forms is a diastereomer of every other form except one. Which is the exception?

options.label: Its own enantiomer, the mirror image
Any form with the same formula
The form with the most stereocenters
Its nearest neighbour on the page

items.explain: A form is a diastereomer of every other configuration excluding its own enantiomer.

items.prompt: Two isomers of a molecule differ only in how groups sit around a double bond. What do they count as?

options.label: Enantiomers, because they are mirror images
Neither, since double bonds have no isomers

items.explain: Double bond isomers are always considered diastereomers, not enantiomers.

items.prompt: Two diastereomers differ from each other at just one stereocenter. What name applies?
items.explain: Diastereoisomers that differ at only one stereocenter are epimers.
